chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a narrative about Musa (peace be upon him): 'My Lord! Surely I stand in need of whatever good You may Send down upon me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He asked for the food.'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Musa mean when he said 'I am in need of whatever good You send down'?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) clarifies that Prophet Musa’s (peace be upon him) plea for 'good' in Quran 28:24 specifically referred to food, highlighting the fundamental human need for sustenance. This interpretation underscores the practical reality that even prophets, in their human state, rely on divine provision for basic physical needs, reinforcing the chapter's theme of human hollowing and dependence on Allah. Such exegetical insights from the Imams provide believers with a deeper understanding of how general Quranic terms can have specific, context-driven meanings.
